messages:
Sam: Heads-up — after landing the new kernel-scorer, we saw a regression on 8xA100 runs for MQA 8->16 batching. p99 went from 72ms -> 110ms on short sequences. Not huge but consistent across clients.
Kira: ugh. Is this on paged-KV or hot-KV profiles?
Sam: Mostly paged-KV workloads (chatty sessions with many short contexts). KV cache lookups show more `page_fault` churn.
Lucas: Can you paste the perf dump?
Sam: Sure — reduced extract:
```
model: gpt-large-mqa
hw: A100-80GB x8
batch: dynamic up to 16
seq: 32
kernel_pick: scorer_v3 (arch-aware weight)
metrics: p50=12ms p95=48ms p99=110ms tokens/s=18k
kv: page_size=64k block=32 fragments=14
```
Kira: Looks like the scorer_v3 is preferring GQA-style kernels for half the traffic even when MQA paths were better for small sequence lengths. scorer_v3 weight function leaned on occupancy heuristics.
Heidi: Did we change the blocksize heuristic? I thought paged KV blocksz was autoclamped to 64 for MQA.
Sam: We did change a threshold: if avg_seq <= 48 prefer smaller blocksz=32 to reduce transfer, but that interacts poorly with the paging prefetch hysteresis.
Aria: Interesting. So smaller blocksz increases fragment count -> more page lookups -> higher tail latency. Might be a prefetch misfire.
Lucas: Can we reproduce with kernel override? Quick test: force kernel=mqa_smallblock vs gqa_packed.
Sam: Ran that:
```
force_kernel=mqa_smallblock -> p99=98ms
force_kernel=gqa_packed    -> p99=75ms
```
Kira: So gqa_packed is still better for that specific HW & batch. scorer choosing mqa_smallblock was wrong.
Heidi: Maybe our cost model underestimates cache metadata overhead. It models token compute but not page table walk.
Aria: Proposal: add a KV-fragment penalty term to scorer that scales with fragment_count * page_fault_rate_est. Also clamp blocksize choices to avoid <48 when avg_seq variance < 0.2.
Sam: I like the penalty. Also we should improve autotune sampling: currently it samples kernels per model-version per hour; increase sampling to per 15min during canary so we detect regressions faster.
Kira: Agreed. Also add a cheap runtime probe that measures page_faults per 1000 tokens and expose on kernel decision trace.
PerfBot: [auto] Canary test results uploaded: build/1234. delta_p99=+38ms (mqa_smallblock on A100), delta_tokens/s=-12%. See /perf/canaries/3465001234.
Lucas: I'll instrument the scorer locally and try the KV penalty patch. Quick sketch:
```
score = base_latency_est + alpha*occupancy_penalty + beta*fragment_count*page_fault_est
beta ~ 0.6 first pass
```
Heidi: Be careful with beta across archs — H100's MMU behavior changes page fault cost. Use arch multiplier.
Aria: Also consider adding a hysteresis window for kernel switching: require sustained win for 3 samples before switching traffic. That avoids flapping from noisy probes.
Sam: Action items: Lucas + Kira pair on scorer patch (beta arch-multiplier, trace), Heidi to add canary sampling frequency change, Aria to add hysteresis gate. We'll run a 6-hour canary.
Kira: I'll also run a synthetic with high fragment counts to stress prefetch fallback paths.
Sam: Thanks. If the fix reduces p99 under canary to within +5ms of stable, we'll roll.
Aria: FYI — I'll add a dashboard panel for "kv_page_faults / 1k tokens" so ops can see it.
PerfBot: [auto] Ticket created: RWINF-8523 "scorer_v3: add KV fragment penalty + hysteresis" assigned to Lucas.
Lucas: Starting on patch now, will post logs when I have a prototype.
Sam: Thanks all :thumbsup:
